$comment: ONTOLOGY SCHEMA for the BMS minimized V-model. Wired via
`[needs] schema_definitions_from_json = "schemas.json"` in ubproject.toml and
checked by `ubc schema validate` and by the sphinx-needs build.
THIS FILE HOLDS ONLY WHAT A NEED TYPE CANNOT DECLARE. Each type's fields and its
OUTGOING links are declared on the type in ubproject.toml
(`[needs.types.<type>.fields.<name>]`, `[needs.types.<type>.links.<name>]`): a
vocabulary, a pattern, a required field (`nullable = false`), the types a link may
point to (`target_types`), how many links a need holds (`minItems` / `maxItems`).
Both tools check those per need from the declaration alone, so a rule here
restating one would be a second copy to drift. What is left:
id-prefix-*        each type's id prefix. `id` is not a field a need type's
entry may declare (both tools refuse the entry), and the
type's `prefix` only seeds generated ids. `violation`.
coverage-*-back    the five INCOMING obligations of the `direction = "both"`
trace edges. An entry on a back link (`traces_to_back`) is
refused by both tools; `network_back` is the only construct
that reaches incoming links. `warning` -- see below.
field-gap-category the gate's category vocabulary at `warning`: a declared enum
is a violation, and a need type's entry has no severity.
field-req-asil     ASIL presence on `req` at `warning`: `nullable = false` would
not report a req without an ASIL, it would not create it.
Put a rule here only when no declaration can carry it.
FORWARD IS DECLARED, BACKWARD IS A WARNING HERE. Both directions come from the
same `direction = "both"` trace edge, and they are not the same:
An OUTGOING obligation is owed by the need being authored, at the moment it is
authored. A req written without `traces_to` is wrong on the spot, and the author
can fix it without touching anything else. It is the type's `minItems = 1` in
ubproject.toml, a violation.
An INCOMING obligation is owed by a LATER STAGE. Every backward rule below spans
a `depends_on` boundary -- arch <- refines is owed by `swreqs`, which by
construction runs after `archs` -- so it is UNMET BY CONSTRUCTION for as long as
the downstream stage is pending. That is not a defect in the graph, it is the
workflow in motion. `warning`.
This was learned the hard way: the five backward rules started as violations
because a census of a COMPLETE graph found them all satisfied. The moment three
arch elements were authored for a stream whose swreqs did not exist yet,
`coverage-arch-refines-back` failed the build on three needs that were exactly
where the workflow expected them to be. A snapshot of a finished V says nothing
about the states it passes through. Incomplete coverage is `ubc agent gaps`'s
whole job: it reports each as a tracked `gap` need and drives `ubc agent next` to
the stage that owes the work. This file re-reports them so they surface in an
editor too; it should not also be the thing that fails a publish.
WARNING IS NOT FREE, THOUGH -- `ubc check` EXITS 1 ON A WARNING, not only on an
error, and it is a hard CI gate. So a backward rule that fires turns CI red even
at `warning`. Two things follow, and both are already in place:
- The project's ONE STANDING demo gap (REQ_CELL_BALANCING_WINDOW, whose stream
has not reached the archs stage) is exempted in ubproject.toml by a
`[[lint.message-ignores]]` entry pinned to that need's message. Scoped that
tightly on purpose: a plain `[lint] ignore` of the code would blank the whole
family out of `ubc schema validate` too, leaving these five rules firing
nowhere. With the message-ignore they still report there, and in the editor.
- conf.py suppresses the same subtype for the `-W` publish. That one CANNOT be
narrowed -- Sphinx `suppress_warnings` matches type.subtype only, with no
message matching -- so the publish gate is deliberately the blunt one.
network_back.<link>.contains + minContains is the construct for incoming coverage.
Incoming links are not locally visible: a `local` rule on a declared incoming
field name (`satisfied_by`, `verifies_back`, ...) matches nothing and silently
passes. Probed and confirmed -- never reach for `local` on an incoming link.
A `local` presence rule needs `required`: `properties` constrains a key only when
it is present, so a constraint alone silently passes on a need that lacks the key.
TWO KEYWORDS THAT LOOK PORTABLE AND ARE NOT. ubCode accepts both; sphinx-needs
rejects both, and the file is consumed by BOTH engines:
- `not` inside a `select` allOf element -- `ubc check` flags this one as
config.schema_sphinx_needs_incompatible.
- `not` inside a `local` field constraint -- `ubc check` does NOT flag it;
only sphinx-build does, as a hard NeedsConfigException. Prefer a positive
`pattern`.
So `ubc check` passing is not sufficient: run the Sphinx build too.
A SYNTAX ERROR ANYWHERE DISABLES THE WHOLE FILE (ubc reports it against the
pseudo-need `__config__` and applies no rule at all), so re-run both validators
after every edit rather than trusting a clean build.

schemas.message: DECLARED: [needs.types.user_story] gives user_story the prefix US_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [needs.types.req] gives req the prefix REQ_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [needs.types.arch] gives arch the prefix ARCH_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [needs.types.swreq] gives swreq the prefix SWREQ_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [needs.types.impl] gives impl the prefix IMPL_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [needs.types.test] gives test the prefix TEST_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [needs.types.test_result] gives test_result the prefix TRES_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [needs.types.risk] gives risk the prefix RISK_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [needs.types.decision] gives decision the prefix DEC_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [needs.types.gap] gives gap the prefix GAP_, which only seeds generated ids; a need type cannot declare its `id`, so the prefix is checked here.
DECLARED: [[needs.types]] gives change_request the prefix CR_, and `ubc agent change plan` refuses a chosen id without it.

DECLARED (stage `reqs`, direction=both): every user_story must be decomposed into at least one req. OBSERVED 4/4, fan-in 1..7. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by a later stage and is unmet by construction while that stage is pending -- see the FORWARD IS DECLARED, BACKWARD IS A WARNING HERE note in $defs._readme.

DECLARED (stage `swreqs`, direction=both): every arch must be refined by at least one swreq, so no component is left without stated behaviour. OBSERVED 14/14, fan-in 1..4. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by a later stage and is unmet by construction while that stage is pending -- see the FORWARD IS DECLARED, BACKWARD IS A WARNING HERE note in $defs._readme.

DECLARED (stage `code`, direction=both): every swreq must be implemented. OBSERVED 23/23, exactly one impl each. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by a later stage and is unmet by construction while that stage is pending -- see the FORWARD IS DECLARED, BACKWARD IS A WARNING HERE note in $defs._readme.

DECLARED (stage `tests`, direction=both): every swreq must be verified. OBSERVED 23/23, fan-in 1..3. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by a later stage and is unmet by construction while that stage is pending -- see the FORWARD IS DECLARED, BACKWARD IS A WARNING HERE note in $defs._readme.

DECLARED (stage `archs`, direction=both): every req should be satisfied by at least one arch. BACKWARD, so `warning`, not `violation`: this is owed by the `archs` stage, which by construction runs after `reqs`, so a req authored before its architecture exists is exactly where the workflow expects it to be -- see the FORWARD IS DECLARED, BACKWARD IS A WARNING HERE note in $defs._readme. The finding is `ubc agent gaps`'s to own; it reports it as a tracked gap need and points `ubc agent next` at the stage that owes the work. Not carved out by id either: a carve-out would need `not` in `select`, which sphinx-needs rejects, and an id-free carve-out would silently stop checking whole streams.

WARNING, NOT VIOLATION, ON PURPOSE. These are the seven categories the 0.34 engine emits, plus `change_incomplete` from `ubc agent change`, per CATEGORIES in tools/import_gaps.py -- but that importer renders an UNKNOWN category generically rather than rejecting it, because `ubc agent` is alpha and "a gate finding must never be dropped because this table has not caught up with the engine". A violation here would invert that: a newer engine emitting a category not listed here would fail the build instead of reporting the gap. At `warning` the drift is surfaced -- go add the new category to CATEGORIES and to this list -- while the finding still lands. This is also why `gap`'s declaration of gap_category in ubproject.toml (`[needs.types.gap.fields.gap_category]`) carries no enum: a declared enum is a violation, and a need type's entry has no severity.

Each requirement states its ASIL (QM or A to D). PRESENCE only -- the VALUE is constrained by `req`'s own declaration, `[needs.types.req.fields.asil]` in ubproject.toml. Warning, not violation: a new requirement is often written before its safety classification is known. This is the one presence check that is NOT declared on the type: `nullable = false` there would not report a req without an ASIL, it would not create it at all, and the draft-requirement skill writes none.
